reconstruction_choices: This execution-semantics learning diagnostic uses explicitly revised execution semantics. It is not literal paper behavior, an effective baseline, or a safety guarantee. Corridor containment remains unresolved; development selection is not held-out evidence and does not authorize delay experiments.

This fresh reconstruction lineage explicitly selects paper_environment_execution_refresh.json and current_state_refresh ordinary-flyby guidance. Preserve initialization 61001, training scenario stream 610000 onward, sampling/shuffle streams and the original 12 development cases. This is a guidance-formula correction, not a confirmed author 2026 implementation or an effective baseline. Resolved configurations and navigation_refresh.py scientific identity remain strict; old native-cached checkpoints are incompatible and must not be migrated or relabeled.

One native environment is reset for fresh training seeds training_scenario_seed_start + completed_episodes. No pre-birth transitions are fabricated. Arrival, deadline failure and any explicitly configured route-exhaustion failure terminate that aircraft with zero bootstrap; failed-route exposure remains reported and cannot be interpreted as a safety improvement.

Initialization, Python and NumPy use training_seed; training action sampling and PPO shuffling use separate saved CPU torch.Generator streams. Evaluation samples use dev_action_seed_base + case seed, reset identically for each policy checkpoint.

Preserve all 12 original development cases cycling 3/4/5 corridors. NR and sampled policy share each exact generated scenario. NR is cached once per geometry per job. Optional argmax is reported separately and never selects the checkpoint.

Aggregate rates divide summed unordered pair-seconds by summed flight-hours, retaining failed-flight exposure. Among models with completed/planned >=0.95, lower NMAC seconds per flight-hour wins, then lower LoWC. Before eligibility, higher completed fraction wins, then NMAC and LoWC. Exact ties keep the earlier checkpoint.

Run initial evaluation before updating, periodic evaluation every 25 completed episodes and final evaluation of the latest model when time allows. Any --eval-limit prefix is explicitly a smaller development diagnostic and remains part of strict checkpoint compatibility.

The initial target is 300 completed episodes with a 600-second inner budget; --episodes is the total target including resume. The controller bounds each job against the active research-block deadline and leaves startup/exit margin in the outer launcher.

Before starting another episode, reserve measured evaluation time and save grace. Check the inner cutoff between decisions. An interrupted episode is discarded, its pre-episode RNG states restored, and its scenario seed remains next; it is not updated or reported completed.

Atomic latest.pt is written initially, every 5 completed episodes and on orderly exit. best.pt follows the predeclared development selection; latest.pt embeds the selected best checkpoint. Scope, exact effective configurations and software/source versions must match on resume; checkpoints from literal execution are not relabeled or silently migrated.
